review.reason: Deploy 5767 (LOG-0007) put the Project Quartz production endpoint live with safety_classifier=off, and monitoring (LOG-0035) shows 0% classifier coverage for 9 days, while the only approved change (CR-4972, LOG-0005) covers Project Heron, not Quartz.

Pellucid Biotech's training opt-out was effective 2026-06-22 (LOG-0008), yet shard cs-3942 from that customer, ingested through 2026-06-30, was included in run-4718's training data mix (LOG-0021), and the opt-out filter later removed 0 records (LOG-0033), so data provided during the opt-out (2026-06-22 to 06-30) was used for training.
run-1552 used 16,384 GPUs for 10 days (about 3.93M GPU-hours, above the 1.9M threshold in LOG-0009), yet LOG-0021 says the quarterly compute report does not list it.

Deploy 7519 (LOG-0030) put the Project Cinder production endpoint live with safety_classifier=off, and LOG-0045 confirms 0% classifier coverage for 9 days, while the only approved change (CR-7828, LOG-0006) covers Project Heron, not Cinder.

Pellucid Biotech's opt-out took effect 2026-04-08 (LOG-0010), yet training run run-5482 included shard cs-4252, which was ingested through 2026-04-28 (LOG-0029), and the opt-out filter removed 0 records (LOG-0032), so data provided during the opt-out was used for training.

run-2812 (6,144 GPUs × 18 days ≈ 2.65M GPU-hours) exceeds the 1.3M threshold and is absent from the report, but that report was filed 2026-04-27, before the run took place in June–July, so the logs show no filed report covering the run's period and no missed listing.

The only classifier-off deploy (LOG-0012, Quartz) was in staging, not production; Basalt's production disablement was approved (CR-2402) and its later production deploy has the classifier on (LOG-0027), and Quartz production shows 100% classifier coverage (LOG-0049).

The only production endpoint with the classifier off is Project Basalt (deploy 7564, LOG-0046), and CR-1213 (LOG-0009) approved disabling it during rollback INC-7564, so this falls under the claim's approved-change exception; the Lumen endpoint has it on, and Basalt coverage returned to 100% after 3 hours (LOG-0056).

The classifier is off on the Project Lumen production endpoint (deploy 2466, 0% coverage in LOG-0019), but CR-1019 approved disabling it (LOG-0004) before the deploy, which fits the claim's "unless a change is approved" exception, and the only other production endpoint, Project Cinder, has it on.

The logs show Corvane Capital's opt-out took effect 2026-04-08 (LOG-0013) and that the only Corvane shard in run-4301 (cs-9196) was entirely ingested before that date (LOG-0034), so the 0 records removed by the opt-out filter (LOG-0038) is consistent with no data provided during the opt-out being used for training.

Pellucid's opt-out took effect 2026-04-27, and the shard cs-2943 data ingested on or after that date was removed from run-3883 by the opt-out filter (LOG-0025) before the cinder-rl-ft-run-3883 job was queued (LOG-0026), and nothing in the logs shows any opted-out data being trained on.

The only customer shard in run-6814 (cs-3247, ingested 2026-03-19 to 2026-05-08) belongs to Brightwater Health, whose agreement permits training (LOG-0017), while the opted-out customer is Tessaly Retail Group (opt-out effective 2026-04-18), and no log shows Tessaly data entering training, so the 0 records removed by the opt-out filter is consistent.

run-6059 was cancelled after 2 days on 16,384 GPUs, so it used about 786,432 GPU-hours, below the 1,900,000 threshold (only the 10-day booking of about 3.9M GPU-hours exceeded it), and the quarterly report was filed 2026-05-22, before the run, so its absence doesn't contradict the claim.

run-1349 (512 GPUs × 60 days ≈ 737,280 GPU-hours) is above the 300,000 threshold, and although the quarterly report does not list it by ID, LOG-0044 says it is covered by project line PL-5474, so it does appear in the report.
The only run missing from the quarterly report, run-9273, used 3,072 GPUs for 28 days, which is about 2,064,384 GPU-hours and below the 4,200,000 GPU-hour threshold, so it did not have to be listed.

The only production endpoint deploys in the logs (LOG-0035 Kestrel and LOG-0036 Lumen) both have safety_classifier=on, monitoring shows 100% classifier coverage for Kestrel production (LOG-0037), and no change requests exist (LOG-0020), so nothing shows the classifier being off on a production endpoint.

The only customer data shown in training is Tessaly's shard cs-6441 in run-2216, and LOG-0007 says Tessaly had a standard agreement with no opt-out (reviewed 2026-06-01), while no log shows any customer with an opt-out in effect whose data was used, so the 0 records removed by the opt-out filter is consistent with the claim.

The only run above the 600,000 GPU-hour threshold is run-4612 (4,096 GPUs × 14 days ≈ 1.38M GPU-hours), and LOG-0029 shows it listed in the quarterly compute report, while all other jobs are small 1-GPU jobs far below the threshold.

Both production endpoint deploys (Juniper, LOG-0023; Lumen, LOG-0031) show safety_classifier=on, monitoring reports 100% classifier coverage for Juniper production (LOG-0053), and no change requests exist, so no endpoint is shown running without the classifier.

The only record of Oakhaven Insurance's terms (LOG-0007, reviewed 2026-04-05) says standard agreement with no opt-out, and no log shows an opt-out taking effect, so the shard's use in run-4024 and the filter removing 0 records do not show a violation.
